note: Former sand and gravel quarry just north of Colfax, right off I-80 Exit 155, run by the non-profit Colfax Park & Auxiliary Board under a 28E agreement with the City of Colfax. The RV park is a new loop of back-in pads south of the park's main road; the separate primitive campground to the south takes only tents and campers under 15 ft, and other RVs overflow to the south side of the main parking lot. Quarry lakes with electric motors only and kayak rentals; no swimming. The north row of RV pads looks across the park road and about 140 m of open grass to the north lake. --Claude
summary: The park's own pages confirm the 40-stall RV park with 30/50A at each site, $40/night, showers, fill spigots, dump, April 1-Oct 31 and online booking on Firefly (14-day limit). The '~$10/site' and 'city-operated' note text were wrong and were dropped. Lakeview stands; phone 515-478-6272 found. The park is run by a 501(c)(3) board (ownership question flagged).
flags: OWNERSHIP: possibly private, not local. The FAQ says 'The land was donated by Martin Marietta to the Colfax Park & Auxiliary Board ... A 28E agreement was setup between the City of Colfax and Park & Auxiliary board in which the board will setup and operate the park and the city will annex the land and help provide police protection, insure', and the home page says 'We are a 501(c)(3) non-profit' and 'Our park is funded entirely by donations, events we host, and building/land rental'. The home page's About blurb contradicts the FAQ on the donee ('donated by Martin Marietta in April of 2014 to the City of Colfax'). Under the Wabash & Erie rule (a non-profit corporation running the park is private) it would be private; the private gates pass anyway: own website + phone, posted $40, Google 4.3 / 167 ('Quarry Springs Park') and 4.0 / 12 ('Quarry Springs RV Park & Campground').

WATERFRONT: 'lakeview' kept. On NAIP the RV loop (two rows of back-in pads, ~41.6880,-93.2368) lies just south of the park's main gravel road; north of the road an open grass field with scattered shrubs runs about 140 m to the beach of the north quarry lake (several hundred metres across, a lake). The north-row pads look across both roads and that field to the water: a view, with roads between, so not on-water. The west lake is ~150 m+ beyond the parking lot; the south lake borders the primitive campground, which EKKO may not use.
